templates.pattern: In a class of [N] students, [P1] ranks [A]th from top in Hindi and [B]th from top in English. If [C] students rank above [P1] in both subjects, how many students rank above [P1] in at least one subject?
templates.explanation: By inclusion-exclusion: above in Hindi=(A-1), above in English=(B-1), above in both=C. At least one = (A-1)+(B-1)-C

templates.pattern: In a queue of [N] people, [P1] is [A]th from front. [P2] is [B]th from back. [P3] is exactly between [P1] and [P2]. [P4] is [K] places behind [P3]. [P5] is [M] places ahead of [P4]. What is [P5]'s position from the front?

Five friends [P1]-[P5] complete tasks at different speeds. [P1] completes a task in [D1] days. [P2] is [K]% faster than [P1]. [P3] is [M]% slower than [P2]. They all work together. In how many days do they complete [TASKS] identical tasks (only [P1],[P2],[P3] work)?
templates.explanation: [P2] rate = (1+K/100)/D1. [P3] rate = (1+K/100)*(1-M/100)/D1. Combined days = TASKS/(sum of rates)

templates.pattern: In an exam, [P1] scored [S1] marks and ranked [R1]th. [P2] scored [S2] marks. If every [STEP] marks difference = 1 rank difference, what is [P2]'s rank?

A sequence of events: Event 1 at [T1] hrs, Event 2 is [D12] hours after Event 1. Event 3 is [D23] hours after Event 2. Event 4 is [D34] hours before Event 5. Event 5 is at [T5] hrs. How many hours is the gap between Event 3 and Event 4?
templates.explanation: Event3 time = T1+D12+D23. Event4 time = T5-D34. Gap = Event4 - Event3 = T5-D34-(T1+D12+D23)

templates.pattern: In a class, [P1] says 'I am [A]th from top.' [P2] says 'I am [B]th from bottom.' [P3] says 'There are [C] students between [P1] and me, and I am below [P1].' [P4] says 'I am [D] ranks above [P3].' What is [P4]'s rank from top?
In a row of [N] people, [P1] is [A]th from left, [P2] is [B]th from right. After [P1] moves [K] places right and [P2] moves [M] places left, how many people are now between them?
templates.explanation: [P1] new pos from left = A+K. [P2] new pos from left = N-B+1-M. Between = [P2]new-[P1]new-1

templates.pattern: Three athletes [P1],[P2],[P3] run laps. [P1] takes [T1] min/lap, [P2] takes [T2] min/lap, [P3] takes [T3] min/lap. They start together. After [DUR] minutes, how many times has [P1] lapped [P3] (i.e., how many extra laps has [P1] completed over [P3])?
templates.explanation: [P1] laps = floor(DUR/T1). [P3] laps = floor(DUR/T3). Difference = floor([DUR]/[T1]) - floor([DUR]/[T3])

templates.pattern: In a test, [P1] ranks [A]th from top. [P1] says: 'If [K] students who scored less than me had scored more, my rank would be [B]th.' How many students scored exactly the same as [P1]?
templates.explanation: If K lower-ranked students beat [P1], rank becomes B. So B = A + K - same_scorers + 1... solving: same scorers = A+K-B+1... Simplified: B-A = K - (tied-1) → tied = K-(B-A)+1

templates.pattern: A project timeline: Phase 1 starts on [D1] Jan and lasts [W1] weeks. Phase 2 starts immediately after and lasts [W2] weeks. Phase 3 starts [G] days after Phase 2 ends and lasts [W3] weeks. On what date (day of year) does Phase 3 end?

[N] students sit in a row for photos. [P1] is [A]th from left. [P2] is [B]th from right. Photographer says: 'If you both move [K] places towards each other, you will be adjacent.' Is the statement correct? Currently how many people are between them?
templates.explanation: Between = N-A-B = [N]-[A]-[B]. After moving K each, gap = N-A-B-2K. Adjacent means gap=1 → N-A-B-2K=1 → verify.

templates.pattern: In a sports meet, [P1] finishes [A] seconds behind the winner. [P2] finishes [B] seconds behind [P1]. [P3] finishes [C] seconds ahead of [P2]. The winner's time is [WT] seconds. What is [P3]'s time?

In a class of [N] students, [P1] is [A]th from top. After results, [X] students who were below [P1] are now above [P1] and [Y] students who were above [P1] are now below [P1]. What is [P1]'s new rank?
templates.explanation: New rank = Old rank + Students below who went above - Students above who went below = [A]+[X]-[Y]

templates.pattern: Two persons [P1] and [P2] start from opposite ends of a [D] km road and walk towards each other. [P1] walks at [S1] km/h, [P2] at [S2] km/h. They meet after [T] hours. After meeting, [P1] continues and reaches [P2]'s starting point. How long did the entire journey take for [P1]?
templates.explanation: Total journey = D km at S1 km/h = D/S1 = [D]/[S1] hours

templates.pattern: In a ranking, [P1] ranks [A]th from top. [P2] says 'I am ranked half of [P1]'s rank from the bottom.' Total students = [N]. What is [P2]'s rank from top?
templates.explanation: [P1] rank from bottom = N-A+1. [P2] rank from bottom = (N-A+1)/2. [P2] from top = N-(N-A+1)/2+1

templates.pattern: In a sequence of events on a single day, [E1] happens at [T1]:00. [E2] happens [A] hours and [B] minutes after [E1]. [E3] happens [C] hours before [E2]. [E4] happens [D] minutes after [E3]. How many minutes before [E2] does [E4] happen?
templates.explanation: [E3] is C hrs before [E2]. [E4] is D mins after [E3]. [E4] before [E2] = C*60-D = [C]*60-[D] minutes

templates.pattern: In an office, [P1] joined [Y1] years ago. [P2] joined [K] years after [P1]. [P3] joined [M] years after [P2]. [P4] joined [N] years after [P3]. If [P4] joined this year ([CY]), how many years ago did [P1] join?
templates.explanation: [P1] joined K+M+N years before [P4]. Since [P4] joined this year, [P1] joined [K]+[M]+[N] years ago

templates.pattern: In a class, [P1] ranks [A]th from top and [B]th from bottom. [P2] ranks [C]th from top. [P3] is ranked such that the number of students between [P2] and [P3] equals the number between [P1] and [P2]. [P3] is below [P2]. What is [P3]'s rank from the bottom?
templates.explanation: N=A+B-1. Between [P1]&[P2] = A-C-1. [P3] rank from top = C+(A-C-1)+1+1 = A+1. From bottom = N-A-1+1 = B-1... Correct: [P3] from top = 2*C+(A-C-1)+1... Let gap = A-C-1. [P3] top = C+gap+1+1 = A+1. From bottom = N-(A+1)+1 = B-1

templates.pattern: A train leaves station A at [SH]:[SM] and reaches station B at [EH]:[EM]. The train stops for [STOP] minutes total at intermediate stations. Distance = [DIST] km. What is the actual running speed (excluding stop time) in km/h?
templates.explanation: Running time = Total time - Stop time = (EH-SH) hrs - STOP/60 hrs. Speed = DIST/Running time

templates.pattern: In a class of [N] students, [P1] ranks [A]th. In a different subject, same students appear and no two get the same rank. The minimum possible rank of [P1] in the combined merit (sum of both ranks) is [MIN_RANK]. What is this minimum combined rank sum for [P1]?
templates.explanation: Minimum combined rank = A (first subject) + 1 (best possible in second) = A+1 = [A]+1

templates.pattern: Seven persons [P1]-[P7] are in a queue. [P1] is [A]th from front. Every 5 minutes, the first person in the queue is served and leaves. [P2] joins the end of the queue every 3 minutes. Starting now, after [T] minutes, what position is [P1] in?
templates.explanation: People served in T mins = floor(T/5). [P1] new position = max(1, A - floor(T/5))

templates.pattern: In a league of [N] teams, each team plays every other team once. Rankings are by points (Win=3, Draw=1, Loss=0). [P1]'s team won [W] matches, drew [D] matches. They played all [N-1] matches. What is [P1]'s team's points and how many did they lose?
templates.explanation: Points = 3W+D = 3*[W]+[D]. Losses = (N-1)-W-D

templates.pattern: In a row of [N] persons, [P1] is [A]th from left. [P2] is [B]th from right. They swap. Now [P3] says: '[P1] is now [C] places to my left and [P2] is [D] places to my right.' What is [P3]'s position from left?
templates.explanation: After swap: [P1] is at B's old position = N-B+1 from left. [P3] = [P1]_new + C = N-B+1+C

templates.pattern: A meeting has [M] agenda items. Item 1 takes [T1] min. Each subsequent item takes [STEP] minutes more than the previous. The meeting starts at [SH]:[SM]. After a [BRK] minute break after item [K]th, what time does item [TARGET]th end?
templates.explanation: Sum of first TARGET items = TARGET*T1 + STEP*(0+1+...+(TARGET-1)). Add break after Kth. End time = Start + items_time + break

templates.pattern: In a qualifying exam, [P1] ranks [A]th from top. For the final selection, only top [PCT]% qualify. Total students = [N]. [P1] needs to improve by at least [GAP] ranks to qualify. Is [P1] currently qualified? What is the cutoff rank?
templates.explanation: Cutoff rank = floor(N*PCT/100) = floor([N]*[PCT]/100). [P1] rank [A] vs cutoff. Qualified if A <= cutoff.
